newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian paramilitary chief gets 30-year sentence.
newsitem.headline: Colombian paramilitary chief gets 30-year sentence.

text.p: The founder of Colombia's leading right-wing paramilitary group was sentenced in absentia on Friday to 30 years in prison for his role in a peasant massacre and the kidnap-murder of a prominent politician.

Court sources said the ruling against Fidel Castano, leader of the dreaded Peasant Self-Defence Force of Cordoba and Uraba (ACCU), was handed down by a judge in the northwest city of Medellin, whose identity would not be revealed out of fear of violent reprisals.

Castano has been missing since 1994, shortly after the Supreme Court upheld an earlier 20-year sentence against him for the murder of 17 banana workers in Uraba, a notoriously violent region near Colombia's border with Panama.
The sentence issued Friday condemned him for the masssacre of 43 peasants in a separate incident in Uraba in January 1990, and for the kidnapping and murder of a leading senator in January 1988.
The ACCU is currently run by Fidel Castano's younger brother Carlos, who claims Fidel was killed by leftist gunmen while on an arms-buying trip in the jungles of Panama.
Human rights groups accuse the ACCU of killing labour activists and suspected leftist rebel sympathisers with impunity and with the tacit support of Colombia's military.
Military officials deny the allegation and say the ACCU is an outlaw group whose members will one day be tracked down and either killed or taken prisoner.
